newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - JAN 21.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - JAN 21.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- It is unlikely that the two opposition parties Smallholders and MDNP are unlikely to gather the required number of MPs' signatures for a vote of confidence against Prime Minister Gyula Horn.

- The head of the Central Investigative Office told a special parliamentary inquiry that lawyer Marta Tocsik did transfer part of her disputed success fee to companies that have close ties with the two ruling parties.
- Polioce uncovered a group of car thieves.
- Privatisation agency APV Rt has signed a contract with the social insurance funds about the transfer of 64 billion forints worth of assets.
- Visiting Polish President Aleksandr Kwasniewski said he hopes both Poland and HUngary could become EU members within two years.
